title: A common Noetherian model for base and closed-fibre flatness
statement: Let $R,S,S\prime$ be commutative local rings with local homomorphisms $R\to S\to S\prime$. Suppose $S$ and $S\prime$ are localizations of finitely presented $R$-algebras [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. Let $M$ be a finitely presented $S\prime$-module, with the restricted $S$- and $R$-actions. Assume $M$ is flat over $R$ and $(S/\mathfrak m_R S)\otimes_S M$ is flat over $S/\mathfrak m_R S$ [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. The zero module is allowed. Then there exist commutative Noetherian local rings $R_0,S_0,T_0$ [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], local homomorphisms $R_0\to S_0\to T_0$, a finite $T_0$-module $N_0$ [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] with restricted $S_0$- and $R_0$-actions, and ring maps $R_0\to R$, $S_0\to S$, such that (i) $N_0$ is flat over $R_0$; (ii) $(S_0/\mathfrak m_{R_0} S_0)\otimes_{S_0}N_0$ is flat over $S_0/\mathfrak m_{R_0}S_0$; (iii) for some multiplicative subset $U$ of $R\otimes_{R_0}S_0$, there is an $R$-linear isomorphism $U^{-1}(R\otimes_{R_0}S_0)\cong S$; and (iv) writing $C=S\otimes_{S_0}T_0$, there is a $C$-module structure on $S\otimes_{S_0}N_0$ restricting to its usual $S$-module structure, a multiplicative subset $V$ of $C$, and an $S$-linear isomorphism $V^{-1}(S\otimes_{S_0}N_0)\cong M$. Here the localizations in (iii) and (iv) are module localizations [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]. For $R:\mathrm{Type}\ u$, $S:\mathrm{Type}\ v$, $S\prime:\mathrm{Type}\ w$, $M:\mathrm{Type}\ t$, the three stage rings may lie in $\mathrm{Type}\ (\max(u,v,w))$ and the stage module in $\mathrm{Type}\ t$. This conclusion does not assert $S_0$ flat over $R_0$ or $N_0$ flat over $S_0$.

proof.text: (Claim L: a localization of a module flat over the base is flat over the base.) Let $A\to C$ be a ring map, $W\subseteq C$ a multiplicative subset and $P$ a $C$-module which is flat as an $A$-module [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]; let $W^{-1}P$ be its localization [def-weil-pbc-module-localization], an $A$-module through $A\to C$. Then $W^{-1}P$ is a flat $A$-module. Indeed, let $u:X_1\to X_2$ be an injective $A$-linear map. Since $P$ is flat over $A$, $1_P\otimes u:P\otimes_AX_1\to P\otimes_AX_2$ is injective, and it is $C$-linear for the $C$-module structures through $P$. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact] applied to the exact sequence $0\to P\otimes_AX_1\to P\otimes_AX_2$, the map $W^{-1}(1_P\otimes u)$ is injective. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-tensor-over-base] (with the ring map $A\to C$, $T=W$, the $C$-module $P$ and the $A$-modules $X_1$, $X_2$) there are isomorphisms $W^{-1}(P\otimes_AX_i)\cong W^{-1}P\otimes_AX_i$, natural in $X_i$, so $W^{-1}(1_P\otimes u)$ corresponds to $1_{W^{-1}P}\otimes u$, which is therefore injective. Hence $W^{-1}P$ is flat over $A$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00MO (lemma-another-variant-local-criterion-flatness, line 23921): 'as the localization of a flat module is flat'; used implicitly in the last sentence of the Algebra, Lemma Tag 00R7 (lemma-criterion-flatness-fibre, line 32992), proof

proof.text: (Claim P: flatness passes along a base change followed by a localization.) Let $A\to A'$ and $A\to B$ be ring maps, $B'$ a ring with ring maps $B\to B'$ and $A'\to B'$ agreeing on $A$, such that the induced map $C:=B\otimes_AA'\to B'$, $b\otimes a'\mapsto\bar b\,\bar a'$, is a localization of $C$ at a multiplicative subset $W\subseteq C$. Let $N$ be a $B$-module which is flat as an $A$-module and $N'$ a $B'$-module ($A'$ acting through $A'\to B'$) with a $B$-linear map $N\to N'$ such that $N\otimes_BB'\to N'$, $x\otimes y\mapsto y\bar x$, is an isomorphism. Then $N'$ is a flat $A'$-module. Proof: $P:=N\otimes_AA'$ is a $C$-module ($(b\otimes a')(x\otimes a'')=bx\otimes a'a''$) and a flat $A'$-module by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-module-base-change]. By associativity of the tensor product, $N\otimes_BC\cong P$ ($x\otimes(b\otimes a')\mapsto bx\otimes a'$) and $N\otimes_BB'\cong(N\otimes_BC)\otimes_CB'\cong P\otimes_CB'$, $C$-linearly. Since $C\to B'$ is a localization at $W$, $B'\cong W^{-1}C$ as $C$-algebras [lem-weil-pbc-localization-of-localization] (its first sentence), and [lem-weil-pbc-localization-tensor-over-base] (with the identity ring map of $C$, $T=W$, the $C$-module $C$ and the $C$-module $P$) gives $W^{-1}C\otimes_CP\cong W^{-1}P$. Hence $N'\cong W^{-1}P$ as $C$-modules, so as $A'$-modules, since $A'\to C\to B'$ is the given map $A'\to B'$. By Claim L (step 1, with $A'\to C$, $W$ and $P$), $W^{-1}P$, hence $N'$, is flat over $A'$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00R7 (lemma-criterion-flatness-fibre, line 32992), proof, last sentence ('Then $S=S_\lambda\otimes_{R_\lambda}R$ is flat over $R$, and $M=M_\lambda\otimes_{S_\lambda}S$ is flat over $S$ (since the base change of a flat module is flat)'), corrected: S and M are only localizations of these base changes; and the passage from 'for some $\lambda$' in Lemma 00R6 to 'for all $\lambda$ big enough' in the proof of 00R7

proof.text: (The limit system.) Apply [lem-weil-pbc-limit-tower-essentially-finite-presentation] to $R\to S\to S'$ and $M$, which is allowed by hypotheses (1), (2) [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. We obtain a nonempty directed set $\Lambda$, local rings $(R_\lambda,\mathfrak p_\lambda)$, $S_\lambda$, $S'_\lambda$ with local homomorphisms $R_\lambda\to S_\lambda\to S'_\lambda$, local transition maps, $S'_\lambda$-modules $M_\lambda$ and maps to $R,S,S',M$ with properties (1)-(5) of that node. Since $R_\lambda\to R$ is a local homomorphism of local rings, $\mathfrak p_\lambda$ is the inverse image of $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak m_R$ (the inverse image is a proper ideal containing the maximal ideal $\mathfrak p_\lambda$); likewise $\mathfrak p_\lambda$ is the inverse image of $\mathfrak p_\mu$ under $R_\lambda\to R_\mu$ for $\lambda\le\mu$. For Lean, lift the input rings to a common universe Type (max u v w) before invoking the same-universe limit-tower theorem and transport the resulting comparison maps through the lift equivalences; stage modules remain in Type t.

proof.text: (Noetherian local stages.) The ring $\mathbf Z$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] (every ideal is $n\mathbf Z$). If $T_0$ is a Noetherian ring and $T_1$ is essentially of finite type over $T_0$ [def-weil-pbc-essentially-finite-type-algebra], i.e. $T_1\cong W^{-1}B$ with $B$ of finite type over $T_0$, then $B$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] and $W^{-1}B$ by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian]. Applying this three times with property (2) of step 3: $R_\lambda$, $S_\lambda$ and $S'_\lambda$ are Noetherian local rings. Put $\hat S_\lambda=S_\lambda/\mathfrak p_\lambda S_\lambda$, $\hat S'_\lambda=S'_\lambda/\mathfrak p_\lambda S'_\lambda$ and $\hat M_\lambda=M_\lambda/\mathfrak p_\lambda M_\lambda$. They are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-image-noetherian]; they are local, because $\mathfrak p_\lambda S_\lambda$ lies in the maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_{S_\lambda}$ ($R_\lambda\to S_\lambda$ is local), so $\hat S_\lambda\ne0$ and its ideals not containing $1$ lie in $\mathfrak m_{S_\lambda}/\mathfrak p_\lambda S_\lambda$ (same for $S'_\lambda$). The maps $S_\lambda\to S'_\lambda$, $S_\lambda\to S_\mu$, $S'_\lambda\to S'_\mu$, $M_\lambda\to M_\mu$ ($\lambda\le\mu$) pass to the quotients, since $\mathfrak p_\lambda$ maps into $\mathfrak p_\mu$ (step 3), and the induced ring maps $\hat S_\lambda\to\hat S'_\lambda$, $\hat S_\lambda\to\hat S_\mu$, $\hat S'_\lambda\to\hat S'_\mu$ are local homomorphisms; $\hat M_\lambda$ is a finitely generated $\hat S'_\lambda$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] (images of generators of $M_\lambda$, property (3)).

proof.text: ($S'_\lambda\otimes_{R_\lambda}R_\mu\to S'_\mu$ is a localization.) Let $\lambda\le\mu$ and $E=S_\lambda\otimes_{R_\lambda}R_\mu$. By associativity of the tensor product, $S'_\lambda\otimes_{R_\lambda}R_\mu\cong S'_\lambda\otimes_{S_\lambda}E$. By property (4) of step 3, $E\to S_\mu$ is a localization at some $W\subseteq E$; by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-base-change] (with the ring map $E\to D:=S'_\lambda\otimes_{S_\lambda}E$), $D\to D\otimes_ES_\mu\cong S'_\lambda\otimes_{S_\lambda}S_\mu$ is a localization at the image of $W$; and $S'_\lambda\otimes_{S_\lambda}S_\mu\to S'_\mu$ is a localization by property (4). By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-of-localization] (1) the composite $S'_\lambda\otimes_{R_\lambda}R_\mu\to S'_\mu$, which is $x\otimes a\mapsto\bar x\,\bar a$, is a localization at a multiplicative subset.

proof.text: ($M_\lambda$ is flat over $R_\lambda$ for $\lambda$ large.) Apply [lem-weil-pbc-colimit-eventually-flat] to the system $A_\lambda=R_\lambda$, $B_\lambda=S'_\lambda$ (with the local homomorphism $R_\lambda\to S_\lambda\to S'_\lambda$), $N_\lambda=M_\lambda$: the rings are Noetherian local (step 4), the transition maps local (step 3), $M_\lambda$ is finitely generated (property (3)), hypothesis (a) holds by step 5 and (b) by property (4); by property (1) the colimits are $A=R$, $B=S'$ with the map $\beta\circ\alpha$, and $N=M$ with its $S'$-module structure. Since $M$ is flat over $R$ (hypothesis (5)), there is $\lambda_0$ with $M_{\lambda_0}$ flat over $R_{\lambda_0}$. For $\mu\ge\lambda_0$, step 2 (Claim P) with $A=R_{\lambda_0}$, $A'=R_\mu$, $B=S'_{\lambda_0}$, $B'=S'_\mu$, $N=M_{\lambda_0}$, $N'=M_\mu$ (hypotheses by step 5 and property (4)) shows that $M_\mu$ is flat over $R_\mu$.

(The fibre system.) proof.text: ($\hat M_\lambda$ is flat over $\hat S_\lambda$ for $\lambda$ large.) Apply [lem-weil-pbc-colimit-eventually-flat] to the system $A_\lambda=\hat S_\lambda$, $B_\lambda=\hat S'_\lambda$, $N_\lambda=\hat M_\lambda$: Noetherian local rings, local maps and finitely generated modules by step 4; hypotheses (a), (b) by step 7 (i); colimits $A=S/\mathfrak mS$, $B=S'/\mathfrak mS'$, $N=M/\mathfrak mM$ by step 7 (ii). Since $M/\mathfrak mM$ is flat over $S/\mathfrak mS$ (hypothesis (4)), there is $\lambda_1$ with $\hat M_{\lambda_1}$ flat over $\hat S_{\lambda_1}$. For $\mu\ge\lambda_1$, step 2 (Claim P) with $A=\hat S_{\lambda_1}$, $A'=\hat S_\mu$, $B=\hat S'_{\lambda_1}$, $B'=\hat S'_\mu$, $N=\hat M_{\lambda_1}$, $N'=\hat M_\mu$ (hypotheses by step 7 (i)) shows that $\hat M_\mu$ is flat over $\hat S_\mu$.

proof.text: Directedness provides a common index above the indices obtained for base flatness and fibre flatness. Put $R_0=R_\lambda$, $S_0=S_\lambda$, $T_0=S\prime_\lambda$ and $N_0=M_\lambda$. The stage rings are Noetherian local, the two maps are local, and $N_0$ is finite. Retain its base flatness and fibre flatness. No nonzero condition is imposed or used.

Property (5) of the limit tower identifies $S$ with a ring localization of $R\otimes_{R_0} S_0$ (using tensor symmetry). The underlying module is the module localization, giving the $R$-linear equivalence in the statement. Put $C=S\otimes_{S_0}T_0$, acting on $S\otimes_{S_0}N_0$ by $(s\otimes t)(s\prime\otimes n)=ss\prime\otimes tn$. Property (5) identifies $S\prime$ with a localization of $C$ at some $V$. Tensor associativity gives $S\prime\otimes_{T_0}N_0\cong S\prime\otimes_C(S\otimes_{S_0}N_0)$. Tensoring with the localized ring is module localization, by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-tensor-over-base] with the identity base map; hence the tower comparison gives $V^{-1}(S\otimes_{S_0}N_0)\cong M$ as $S$-modules. The displayed $C$-action restricts to the usual $S$-action, providing the scalar tower.

theorem exists_noetherian_flat_closedFiber_model
    (R : Type u) (S : Type v) (S' : Type w) (M : Type t)
    [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [CommRing S']
    [IsLocalRing R] [IsLocalRing S] [IsLocalRing S']
    [Algebra R S] [Algebra S S'] [Algebra R S'] [IsScalarTower R S S']
    [IsLocalHom (algebraMap R S)] [IsLocalHom (algebraMap S S')]
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module S' M] [Module S M] [Module R M]
    [IsScalarTower S S' M] [IsScalarTower R S M]
    (P : Type p) (Q : Type q) [CommRing P] [CommRing Q]
    [Algebra R P] [Algebra P S] [IsScalarTower R P S]
    [Algebra R Q] [Algebra Q S'] [IsScalarTower R Q S']
    [Algebra.FinitePresentation R P] [Algebra.FinitePresentation R Q]
    (W : Submonoid P) (V : Submonoid Q) [IsLocalization W S] [IsLocalization V S']
    [Module.FinitePresentation S' M]
    (h_fibre : Module.Flat
      (S ⧸ Ideal.map (algebraMap R S) (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R))
      ((S ⧸ Ideal.map (algebraMap R S) (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R)) ⊗[S] M))
    [Module.Flat R M] :
    ∃ (R₀ S₀ T₀ : Type (max u v w)) (N₀ : Type t)
      (_ : CommRing R₀) (_ : CommRing S₀) (_ : CommRing T₀)
      (_ : IsLocalRing R₀) (_ : IsLocalRing S₀) (_ : IsLocalRing T₀)
      (_ : IsNoetherianRing R₀) (_ : IsNoetherianRing S₀)
      (_ : IsNoetherianRing T₀)
      (_ : Algebra R₀ S₀) (_ : Algebra S₀ T₀) (_ : Algebra R₀ T₀)
      (_ : IsScalarTower R₀ S₀ T₀)
      (_ : IsLocalHom (algebraMap R₀ S₀)) (_ : IsLocalHom (algebraMap S₀ T₀))
      (_ : AddCommGroup N₀) (_ : Module T₀ N₀) (_ : Module S₀ N₀)
      (_ : Module R₀ N₀) (_ : IsScalarTower S₀ T₀ N₀)
      (_ : IsScalarTower R₀ S₀ N₀)
      (_ : Algebra R₀ R) (_ : Algebra S₀ S),
      Module.Finite T₀ N₀ ∧ Module.Flat R₀ N₀ ∧
      Module.Flat
        (S₀ ⧸ Ideal.map (algebraMap R₀ S₀) (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R₀))
        ((S₀ ⧸ Ideal.map (algebraMap R₀ S₀) (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R₀)) ⊗[S₀] N₀) ∧
      (∃ U : Submonoid (R ⊗[R₀] S₀),
        Nonempty (LocalizedModule U (R ⊗[R₀] S₀) ≃ₗ[R] S)) ∧
      (∃ (_ : Module (S ⊗[S₀] T₀) (S ⊗[S₀] N₀))
        (_ : IsScalarTower S (S ⊗[S₀] T₀) (S ⊗[S₀] N₀))
        (U : Submonoid (S ⊗[S₀] T₀)),
        Nonempty (LocalizedModule U (S ⊗[S₀] N₀) ≃ₗ[S] M))
